title: stacked-pr-closure-recovery-corrective-20260730
outOfScope: Deleting a merged stacked branch without a valid Closure Receipt.
Changing unrelated Work Item lifecycle behavior or release state.

sources.reason: Closure rejects merged PR #474 because it assumes every PR base is the repository default branch.

riskAssessment.reason: An incorrectly accepted arbitrary base could delete the wrong branch; the stacked path must be explicit and prove the parent Work Item branch, ancestry, and receipt facts.

acceptance: Default-branch closure remains fail-closed for wrong PR bases.
A stacked PR may close only when its base is a still-identifiable, unclosed Work Item branch that still retains the stacked PR merge commit.
Closure receipts record the actual stacked base and preserve retry behavior if remote deletion fails.
Regression tests cover an accepted stacked closure after the parent advances, a non-Work-Item base rejection, a merge-retention mismatch rejection, and existing direct PR behavior.
guidelines: Default closure protection stays strict; the stacked path must be evidence-based and opt-in by verified repository state.
Branch deletion occurs only after authoritative merged-PR and Closure Receipt validation.

intent.problem: PR #474 correctly merged its corrective change into the still-open WI-10 branch, but ai-close-work-item rejects it because it assumes every merged PR targets the remote default branch. This leaves the corrective branch unclosable before WI-10 can continue to main.
constraints: Do not weaken direct default-branch PR validation.
Do not delete the corrective branch until its receipt is valid.
Require verifiable stacked-base Work Item identity and merge ancestry.
intent.rationale: A narrowly defined stacked-PR closure path prevents both orphan branches and arbitrary-base branch deletion while preserving isolated corrective PRs.
